mcq_choices.rationale: Invents a new applied force to explain the sensation, when in fact no new force acts on the passenger at all.
the passenger tends to maintain velocity
Attributes the lurch to a nonphysical loss of mass rather than to the passenger's own inertia continuing forward.
Misattributes the lurch to a change in gravity's direction rather than to the passenger's tendency to keep moving at the car's original velocity.

parts.prompt:
A passenger lurches forward when a car stops because

A. a forward force appears
B. inertia preserves forward motion
C. the seat removes mass
D. gravity points forward

criteria.description: Select the single scientifically correct answer.
required_evidence: the passenger tends to maintain velocity

review_notes.expected_reasoning: the passenger tends to maintain velocity
known_boundary_cases: Check notation, sign, or limiting-case reasoning.
